PLAYGROUND LESSON · PLAYGROUND · AGES 2–5 YEARS

Tunnel — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches the tunnel — through the dark and out the other side — with the crawl, the hello-call and the brave truth that tunnels always end in light.

What is this?

A tunnel is a tube to crawl through: dark in the middle, light at both ends — hands and knees forward, a hello echo inside, and the exit always ahead.

What does it mean?

The tunnel is the playground’s tiny bravery lesson: a moment of dark, a voice that echoes, and the proof — every single time — that going THROUGH reaches the other side. That proof is worth more than the crawl.

What does the child need to know?

Your child needs three tunnel ideas: crawl forward on hands and knees — the tunnel is not for standing; the CALL works — hello! echoes down the tube and tells everyone where you are; and tunnels END — keep crawling toward the light; the exit is always ahead.

Why this matters

Dark-tunnel confidence is real courage practice in playground portions — and the echo-call adds voice play, turn-taking and the joy of hearing yourself come back.

What it teaches

Crawling coordination in a confined space, voice-echo play, dark-to-light courage, and the through-to-the-other-side completion.

Words to learn

tunnelcrawldarklightechohellothrough

Say this to your child

“"The tunnel goes through the dark and out the other side! Crawl forward on hands and knees… halfway, call HELLO — hear the echo? The tunnel talks back! And the brave truth of every tunnel: it always ENDS — the light is ahead, keep crawling. Through… echo… light. That is the tunnel’s whole promise!"”

Step by step

  1. Show the card: "This is the tunnel — through the dark, out to the light!"
  2. The crawl: hands and knees, forward — the tunnel is a crawling road, head up enough to see.
  3. The call: halfway in, call HELLO — hear the echo bounce back? The tunnel talks! Calling also tells friends where you are.
  4. The brave truth: tunnels always END — the exit is light, and it is always ahead. Keep crawling; the other side is coming.
  5. Play the tunnel games below and close: "crawl, call, through to the light."

Look closer at the picture

On this card the word "Tunnel" stands in big navy capitals inside the rounded frame, with a friendly tunnel illustration below — exactly as the through-tube looks.

Ask your child

"How do we travel in a tunnel? What does the echo do? What is always ahead in a tunnel?"

What your child can say or do

Your child might say: "Hands and knees, crawl!" "HELLO… hello… hello — it echoed!" or the brave one: "Tunnels always end in light!"

Out in the real world

Tunnels curve through every playground — and the through-to-the-light courage transfers to duvets, cardboard boxes and the big world’s underpasses. The echo is free everywhere.

Try it together

Echo Tunnel Run: crawl in, call HELLO at the middle, listen to the bounce, crawl out to the light — arms up: "THROUGH!" Then the two-way round: one crawler at each end, calling echoes to each other, passing with a giggle in the middle. Three throughs, three echoes, one brave ritual. The tunnel’s promise kept, every time.

Understanding check

Ask: "How do we travel? What does the call make? What is always ahead?" Crawl, an echo, the light — three answers and the tunnel is through.

Parent tips

A familiar voice waiting at the EXIT turns dark tunnels into races — the light has a face. And never rush a pause in the middle: waiting in the dark is part of the courage too.

This lesson pairs with the Tunnel flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Playground.
